identified_issues: Quotient stage erasure collapsing distinct operational workflows into a coarse union context ('AUTHORIZED_USER_SESSION')
Identifiability and rank loss between Workflow A (Interactive Operator Session) and Workflow B (Approved Batch Execution)
Privilege escalation allowing unauthorized 'EXECUTE_MUTATION' execution by a Workflow A interactive operator
Violation of the Separation Axiom by conflating distinct workflow support fibers into an undifferentiated cached session object
evidence: Workflow A permission support is strictly limited to {'READ', 'EXPORT_DRAFT', 'REQUEST_APPROVAL'}
Workflow B permission support is defined as {'READ', 'EXECUTE_MUTATION', 'RELOCK'}
Compression middleware combines permissions into ['READ', 'EXPORT_DRAFT', 'REQUEST_APPROVAL', 'EXECUTE_MUTATION', 'RELOCK'] under 'session_type': 'AUTHORIZED_USER_SESSION'
Middleware approved an 'EXECUTE_MUTATION' request submitted by an interactive operator in Workflow A because the action was present in 'combined_permissions'
recommended_action: Eliminate the lossy quotient compression middleware and restore distinct, uncollapsed authorization session contexts for Workflow A and Workflow B. Enforce separate, non-overlapping permission evaluators that verify caller workflow identity directly at the authorization boundary, and add regression tests ensuring that Workflow A sessions strictly reject 'EXECUTE_MUTATION'.
